newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Puerto Rico moves toward telco privatization.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico moves toward telco privatization.

text.p: Lawmakers in Puerto Rico approved a bill late Wednesday that paved the way for the sale of the Puerto Rico Telephone Co., which would be one of the largest privatizations in Latin America in recent years.
Members of Puerto Rico's House of Representatives approved the bill 30-17. The U.S. territory's senate also is debating a similar bill, which it is expected to pass next week.
The two bills would then be reconciled and sent to Gov. Pedro Rossello, who put the telephone company up for sale in April.
The telephone company is one of Puerto Rico's most profitable public corporations. Its earnings have increased from $800 million in 1991 to $1.1 billion in 1997.
But it lost its monopoly on local service after the passage of the 1996 Federal Telecommunications Reform Act and government officials felt the company could not compete with the private sector.

Puerto Rico had tried to sell the telephone company in 1990 for about $3 billion, which included assumption of its $1 billion debt --- but the sale fell through because the legislators put so many amendments on legislation to allow the sale that the agreement became unattractive to potential investors.

Among the final bidders at that time were BellSouth Corp and GTE Corp. Companies frequently mentioned as interested in acquiring the company this time around are Telefonica de Espana, Bell Atlantic-NYNEX and AT&T Corp.
The House bill passed Wednesday included several amendments, one of which would prohibit the government from offering any tax exemptions to a potential buyer."
The sale also faces heavy opposition from unions representing 6,200 of the telephone company's 8,000 workers.
